parts.title: Questions 31–35
paragraphs: Mad Cow Disease attacks the {{31}} of the affected cows and causes strange behaviour.
BSE is thought to be caused by prions, which are an infectious type of {{32}}.
Abnormal prions in BSE infected cattle are first found in the small intestines, tonsils and the {{33}} making up the central nervous system.
Humans can take in the abnormal prions when they eat infected beef as the abnormal prions are resistant to the usual {{34}} applied to food, such as heat.
The one American case of CJD was a woman who caught it in {{35}} before going to the US.

parts.title: Questions 36–40
paragraphs: CJD causes rapid loss of mental function and {{36}} due to damage from abnormal prions. It can also possibly be genetically inherited. CJD usually affects younger people (from ages 20 to 70) and the patients’ {{37}} of starting symptoms is in their late 50s. Symptoms include personality changes and problems with coordination. Once symptoms appear, the disorder progresses quickly to {{38}} and death.

The exact causes of BSE are unknown but the first UK cases have indicated that it could come from a prion disease in {{39}} called scrapie. The infected meat was then fed to cattle. Dead cattle with scrapie were also fed to {{40}} making them cannibals. So, we are in turn infected by the disease that we created when we eat infected beef.
